name: Context card persistence backend
description: Stores context cards durably in whichever place they must live, with the same behaviour in a local folder, a vector database or the Quest backend.
purpose: Keeps context cards safe and retrievable wherever a person needs them to live, from a local folder to the Quest backend.
approach: Writes, reads, lists and deletes context cards in the chosen store, with no card lost and none duplicated.
out_of_scope: Deciding which cards suit a turn, and backend-specific logic in card handling.
milestones: 1. The same 14 conformance cases pass on the filesystem, embedded Qdrant and Quest API backends. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The same conformance cases pass against a Qdrant server and the dev Quest API, not only the embedded and fake backends.
knowledge: Persistence is a boundary: card logic lives in the store and a backend only stores and fetches. A listing that silently truncated at a page limit once made a backend fail the volume case. Backend errors must be loud and counted, not swallowed, and card identity is the pair of scope and id so the same id may exist privately and in a team.
measures_of_success: Every conformance case passes on every backend: round trip, overwrite, no loss at volume and across pages, no duplicate, delete including after restart, concurrent writers, change stamp and tolerance of bad input. Standing conditions: Lose no card, create no duplicate, and behave the same on every backend, including after restart, under concurrent writers and across paged listings.
parameters: Backend choice and connection (folder path; vector collection, embedder and vector size or server url; Quest base url, key, timeout and scope), plus the optional scope used for tenant isolation.
inputs: Card ids and card dictionaries for write (a card as defined in docs/explanation/context-assembly.md, What a context card is: id, name, keywords, summary and description, pinned files, typed content references, provenance, usage, scope tags and origin); ids for read, delete and exists.
outputs: Load-all returns a mapping of id to card, read returns a card or nothing, write and delete return success flags, and revision returns a change stamp used to invalidate caches.
effects: Durable writes to the chosen store (atomic files, vector points embedded at write time, or API calls), and for the API backend logged and counted errors.
usage_notes: Pick the backend by where the cards must live and inject it into the card store; every backend must pass the same conformance cases, so none is better when it conforms. Add a backend by implementing the protocol and a harness. A card's fields, its id rules and what is not a card are defined once in docs/explanation/context-assembly.md, What a context card is; docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md covers stores, mounts and copies.

name: Source-change staleness detector
description: Flags the context cards whose source file has changed or disappeared, with a check cheap enough to run routinely and no model call.
purpose: Help the assistant keep its context cards in step with the files they describe, so it does not answer from what used to be true.
approach: Compare each card's recorded source state with the current file and report the cards that no longer match.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether a card's wording is still right once its source has changed.
milestones: 1. Every edited or deleted source file is flagged and no unchanged file is flagged, on the synthetic mutation cases, with the check kept cheap.
knowledge: A modification time and size pair is cheap but misses an edit that keeps the size and restores the time, and flags a merely touched file. A content hash is exact but costs a read. The production store keeps a fast path on modification time, accepting one deliberate miss.
measures_of_success: High precision and recall over synthetic mutation cases: edits and deletes flagged, untouched and merely touched files not flagged. Standing conditions: Flag every changed or deleted file and no unchanged file, and keep the check cheap.
parameters: The repository root for fingerprints and whether a git blob id is used when available.
inputs: A pinned file path (or a set of paths) and the current tree.
outputs: Whether the file is stale, and the stale card list for the path.
effects: None beyond reading files and computing hashes; fingerprints are written when a card is written.
usage_notes: Pin a fingerprint when a card is written, ask on assemble, and decide per deployment whether mtime-preserving edits matter enough to hash every time.

name: Offline card cache and write outbox
description: Keeps the last card listing and every failed write, so a backend outage changes what callers see only by a degraded status and loses no write.
purpose: Keep an assistant working through a card backend outage by serving the last known listing and holding failed writes for replay.
approach: Serve the last known card listing and hold every failed write for replay whenever the card backend is unreachable.
out_of_scope: Sharing one cache between hosts, since the file cache is single-host.
milestones: 1. Outage cases passed by the file cache: 12 of 12, including a cold start during an outage and every failed write replayed. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. Outage cases passed by a cache shared across hosts, so every host serves the same listing.
knowledge: The repository never depends on a cache for correctness, and every backend failure is logged, counted and surfaced as a degraded status. A cold start during an outage is the case that separates a durable cache from a memory one. A file cache is single-host.
measures_of_success: On a card API that can go down, callers see identical behaviour, the stored listing is served on a cold start, and every failed write is replayed. Standing conditions: Keep caller-visible behaviour the same with or without a cache. Keep the outage loud. Keep the listing across restarts. Lose no failed write.
parameters: A cache is passed to the repository as an optional argument; the file cache takes a directory. The seam has no tuning parameters.
inputs: A full or delta listing with its latest update time, and failed writes as card id, card and team id.
outputs: The stored listing with its update time, or none, and the queued writes oldest first.
effects: Stores the listing and an outbox on each call; the durable cache writes files atomically and swallows its own I/O errors.
usage_notes: Choose the durable cache for any lane that must survive an outage across restarts; keep the null cache where failing loudly is wanted. Check the repository's health status to see degradation.

name: Card store growth prevention
description: Stops a card store from compounding: a copy never restates a card the store already holds, and the owner's card limit is enforced loudly, never by silent deletion.
purpose: Keeps a card store proportionate to its sources while it is built and refreshed, so a lane's memory stays a useful size.
approach: Gives each copied card an origin-based id, refuses writes that would compound or exceed the limit, and says so in a notice.
out_of_scope: Deciding which folders a corpus may read, repairing a store that has already grown, and touching a card that another system manages or a person wrote.
milestones: 1. Every card store growth case passes as the runner ships: repeated passes over nested stores add no copy of a copy, and a store at its limit refuses new derived cards with a notice. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. On every card growth case, the store opened as the runner opens it keeps cards per topic at 1.0 and duplicate share at 0, with no topic lost. [met: 2026-10-22] 3. The broken baseline (drop_every_import) and the no_cleanup arm fail the cases the selected implementation passes. [met: 2026-10-22]
knowledge: The copy-import id rule (a namespace of the source root, two dashes, the card id, cut to 200 characters) with copies of copies kept is what compounded (docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md, containment audit defects 1 and 2). Two real stores reached 8,557 and 32,070 cards on 2026-10-05 before any guard existed. Mount mode stops copying for the stores that adopt it. The guards committed on 2026-10-22 (origin ids, a store never its own import source, the write-time id refusal, the one-root refusal, the card limit) are on in the runner. The card limit (adapters/card_limit.py) counts the store's own cards on every repository. It never trims by itself: a store found above it is left as it is and told. On a local folder a new learned or quest card at the limit moves the coldest derived card into _quarantine/limit; on the Quest backend and Qdrant, which cannot set a card aside without deleting shared data, a learned card is admitted over the limit (it cannot be rebuilt from the files) while a new bootstrap card is refused, and the notice says so. Repairing a store that already grew is a different job with a different definition of best, so it is its own solution, repair-a-card-store; both run in the runner side by side.
measures_of_success: Every card_store_growth case passes and every card_growth case keeps one card per distinct topic of its source files for the store opened as the runner opens it, with no topic lost and nothing a person or a run wrote lost. Standing conditions: prevention refuses or does not keep a card; it never deletes one. The card limit is the owner's number and is never silent: it never deletes a card, never trims a store it finds above the limit, and says what fills the store and how to change the limit.
parameters: QAR_MAX_CARDS, the most cards one store owns on any repository, 1000 by default; 0 or unlimited removes the limit. QAR_CARD_MOUNT (copy or mount mode). The folder review and risk gate decide what may be read (choose-what-to-index).
inputs: A corpus tree, the lane's card store, and the stores its bootstrap and refresh would import or mount.
outputs: Cards written only under an id made of their origin; a refused write logged as an error naming the id; the card limit's notice naming what fills the store and how to change the limit.
effects: Refuses writes that would compound or exceed the limit. At the limit on a local folder a learned or quest card moves the coldest derived card into _quarantine/limit (undone by moving the file back); on the Quest backend and Qdrant nothing is removed. The notice goes to the log, the startup callback and the next task's progress feed.
usage_notes: A lane in copy mode should move to mount mode (docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md, Migrating a deployment) so the cause stops. To change the limit set QAR_MAX_CARDS where the lane reads its environment (docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md, The card limit). A store that already inflated is repaired by repair-a-card-store, not by raising or lowering the limit.

name: Card store repair
description: Brings a card store that has grown too large back to one card per distinct topic in its source files, removing only copies it can prove and joining what they held onto the card that keeps it.
purpose: Returns an inflated card store to a size that matches its sources, so searches stay focused and nothing a person or a run wrote is lost.
approach: Plans and applies a tidy of duplicate and surplus cards through one repository interface, keeping a way to undo each change.
out_of_scope: Stopping new copies from being made, choosing which folders a corpus may read, choosing which cards suit a task, removing a card a person wrote or taught or one another system manages, and removing shared data from a hosted store without its owner's opt-in.
milestones: 1. Cards per topic is 1.0 with no duplicates and no topic lost, and nothing a person or a run wrote is lost, on every card_growth case, for the repository tidy on a backend-shaped store. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The same holds for the local folder tidy at open and for the quarantine script. 3. Every removal on a hosted store is undone by its manifest in a test against the real hosted API, not only the in-memory fake.
knowledge: Two real stores reached 8,557 and 32,070 cards on 2026-10-05 and were cleaned by moving cards into _quarantine (scripts/quarantine_cards.py). A compounded copy can be the only copy left, so it is removed only when a surviving card with the same files stays. A store on the Quest backend had no tidy at all: one lane's backend store held 5,488 cards, most of them copy-import ids, cards about excluded nested repositories and same-file duplicates. The repository tidy (adapters/card_store_tidy.py, commits 0d641cb, eab09b4 and d00777b) plans and applies the script's rules through the CardRepository port. A backend has no quarantine folder, so there it deletes, after a full local export that the manifest's undo restores from. The tidy at open of a local folder (self_heal, adapters/card_store_hygiene.py) is on in the runner's builders since commit 1503d38.
measures_of_success: Every card_growth case keeps one card per distinct topic of its source files, loses no topic, keeps the cards a person wrote or taught, the managed card and the notes a run added, and keeps two distinct topics on one file apart. Standing conditions: on a local folder a card is moved into _quarantine, never deleted; on a backend a card is deleted only after a complete export of it is written, only when the owner set card_tidy = apply or ran cards tidy --apply, and every deletion is undone by cards tidy --undo with the run's manifest. Never remove a card a person wrote or taught or another system manages, except a provable compounded copy whose holdings join its keeper. The plan is always said where the lane's owner sees it, with the command.
parameters: RunnerConfig.card_tidy (qar.toml): apply, plan or off; unset applies on a local folder and plans on the Quest backend and Qdrant. cards tidy: --config or --cards-dir, --apply, --merge-topics, --undo with a manifest. The quarantine script: the reasons to apply, the file-set overlap at which two cards count as one, excluded and kept folder prefixes, other stores that cover this one, and dry run or apply. self_heal on a local folder store (on in the runner's builders). QAR_MAX_CARDS decides when the startup tidy is due.
inputs: A card store on any repository, its folder review, and optionally other stores to compare it with.
outputs: A plan (tidy-state/last-plan.json for the startup tidy), a manifest naming every card removed or that would be removed, with its reason and the card that keeps its knowledge, a full export of every card touched, and a sentence on the log, the startup callback and the next task's progress feed.
effects: On a local folder moves card files under the store's _quarantine folder by reason; the store ignores that folder, so the index shrinks and a move is undone by moving the file back. On the Quest backend and Qdrant deletes the cards, after writing their export under the lane's own card folder (tidy-state, mode 600); cards tidy --undo re-creates them from it. Keepers gain the keywords of the cards joined onto them. Moving a card does not remove its vector point.
usage_notes: On a backend read the plan the lane announces (or run cards tidy without --apply), then apply it with the command it gives, or set card_tidy = apply to let the lane do it at startup. Keep the export and manifest: they are the only way back on a backend, and they sit on the lane's disk, so copy them elsewhere before anything happens to that disk. Repair does not stop the next growth; bound-card-growth does.

name: Index scope decision
description: Decides, before anything is read, which folders of a corpus may produce or import cards, keeping dated snapshot copies out while real material stays in.
purpose: Keeps a lane's card memory built from real material, not from dated copies of it sitting in a backups folder.
approach: Decides which folders a corpus may read before any card source reads them, and applies that one decision to every source.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether a single file is readable, and privacy fences, which are set by configuration rather than by this judgement.
milestones: 1. With the folder review unavailable, switched off or failing, no card, import or mount comes from a snapshot series, and the nested store and the docs folder stay indexed. [met: 2026-10-22] 2. The lone-snapshot case passes without blocking a single legitimate nested store. [met: 2026-10-22] 3. One read-only run over a real backups folder of dated snapshots, with the verdicts and the time recorded, by decision.
knowledge: The 2026 backups incident: daily snapshots each carrying a card store, 155 stores with 760,608 cards under one folder. The header of context_folder_review.py: on one real corpus most indexable files were a vendored tree present twice and generated data, and judging folders shallow first collapsed thousands of directories into about a hundred decisions in a few batched calls. A cached verdict on the root once excluded the whole corpus, so the root is never excludable. A deterministic exclusion re-opened by its own children let a generated tree back in, so deterministic verdicts are final. The risk gate (commit ac61f64) is pinned by tests/test_folder_review.py and documented in docs/how-to/context-card-stores.md, The risk gate.
measures_of_success: Every choose_what_to_index case passes for the selected implementation, apart from those marked as known gaps, with no snapshot taken in where it should be kept out, nothing real lost, no index verdict overruled, and review calls that grow with flagged folders, not files. Standing conditions: never exclude the corpus root; a person's verdict in folder_review.json wins; one decision for every card source.
parameters: QAR_FOLDER_REVIEW (on by default; off means no review call, and flagged folders are then kept out); QAR_SKIP_NESTED_REPOS; the risk thresholds (stores, series length, child-structure similarity) and the review's file-count floor, batch size and depths in the two modules.
inputs: A corpus tree (the walk root and its skip list), the lane's card store folder with any cached folder_review.json, the card sources that will ask (file walk, nested and ancestor imports, mounts), and optionally a model provider for the folder review.
outputs: A FolderGate: the set of corpus-relative folders no card source may read, and of those the risk-flagged ones that could not be reviewed, with why; every card source asks it, so its complement is the set of folders and stores allowed to produce or import cards.
effects: Writes folder_review.json in the lane's card store (verdicts, reasons, source, signals), makes batched folder review calls when a provider is given, and logs one warning per run naming any folder kept out unreviewed and the override.
usage_notes: Call folder_gate once per pass and hand the same gate to every card source; never let a new card source walk or import without asking it. To include a folder the gate turned away, set index true for it in folder_review.json (pinned to keep it against the deterministic safeguards). context migrate-imports shows what the gate turned away without writing anything.

name: Card categories and metadata
description: Decides the card metadata and file categories a model writes for context cards, with a model call that is kept only while its measured value outweighs its cost and time.
purpose: Gives a person the card metadata and file categories a model writes for context cards at a cost and delay that its metric accepts.
approach: A prompt declared as a prompt spec makes one model call to write card metadata and place modified files in the cards they belong to.
out_of_scope: Choosing the model tier (choose-a-model-tier) and the surrounding turn or run.
milestones: 1. Its metric has a case set and a recorded result for the current arm and the no-model floor. 2. The model call stays only while it beats the floor on the metric.
knowledge: Proposed 2026-10-28 so that this prompt has a solution and a metric that justify its cost, time and value; not built, so the metric is unmeasured and the current call is a direction, not a measured win.
measures_of_success: The metric is read from the cases without invented readings. Standing conditions: Never invent a reading. Add no time before a chat reply.
parameters: The model tier and any cap the module states.
inputs: The text or events the call is given.
outputs: The text or verdict the call returns.
effects: One model call; no write beyond the text it returns.
usage_notes: Selected today: fast_model_labels. The floor is a proposed arm with no model call.

name: Hub card store
description: A hub card-store arm that keeps hub cards in QAR's own CardRepository, so a hub consumer that asks for a card-store gets QAR's persistence (files or the Quest API).
purpose: Let QAR's card persistence stand in the hub's card-store seat instead of the hub's local default.
approach: Maps a hub Card onto the QAR card schema (id, summary, keywords, provenance.source) and delegates add, get, search, delete and count to the repository.
milestones: Declared in QAR's own scope as a child of the hub; production obtains its repository through the hub assembly.
knowledge: The CardRepository interface and the hub CardStore Protocol.
measures_of_success: The card repository conformance cases pass through this store (metric-persist-cards).
parameters: repository: the CardRepository the store keeps its cards in.
inputs: A CardRepository (the repository option of the card-store seat).
effects: Reads and writes the cards behind the repository.
usage_notes: Select it with the card-store seat's selection; production obtains its repository through the hub assembly.

name: QAR topic cards for a folder
description: Proposes the cards for the files of a folder in the card-store record shape and writes nothing; QAR's arm is its own topic bootstrap, where a card groups what several files say about one subject.
purpose: Gives QAR's card store topic cards that group what several files say about one subject, which is what a card is for; a card per file would only be an index of files.
approach: Selects the arm QAR's bootstrap has always used: a model names the areas of the files no card covers and writes a topic card for each, duplicates folded into the cards the store holds. The bootstrap asks the seat for the proposal and keeps the origin stamps, scope tags, card limit, per-folder ceilings, folder gate and upload.
out_of_scope: Where cards are written, who owns them, the card limit and the upload to the Quest backend (bound-card-growth, persist-cards), and finding a file for a task (select-context).
milestones: 1. The bootstrap resolves this seat through QAR's Assembler and writes the same cards as before for the same inputs. 2. QAR's follow check scores the hub's free candidate arms on the topic-level metric.
knowledge: The hub measured one card per file as the best free file finder, and a card store is not a file index: QAR selects topic cards, and a candidate arm is judged on grouping files for a task that names none, with cards per file capped.
measures_of_success: The stored cards are byte-identical to the bootstrap's own for the same corpus and provider (tests/test_bootstrap_via_seat.py), and a batch with one card per file is refused at upload.
parameters: model: the model tier the topic cards are written with; QAR_BOOTSTRAP_MAX_CARDS and the card limit bound what is written.
inputs: The corpus root, the files no card covers, and the cards the store already holds.
outputs: Topic cards as {id, name, keywords, summary, files}, proposed and not written.
usage_notes: Select another arm only for a candidate that beats this one on the topic-level metric and keeps cards per file under the cap; an arm that returns a card per file is a file-finding baseline and is never routed into the card store.
